title: Tracing the Cascade: A Topology-Aware Evaluation Framework for Scientific Agent Hallucinations
abstract: arXiv:2608.00711v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in scientific research, where reliability is critical and the underlying knowledge is densely interconnected. In such settings, hallucinations are particularly damaging: a single erroneous claim on a foundational concept can propagate through multi-step reasoning and corrupt entire trajectories. Existing hallucination benchmarks largely operate at the surface level, treating facts in isolation and relying on uniform accuracy metrics that ignore this topological structure. translated_title: 追踪级联效应：面向科学智能体幻觉的拓扑感知评估框架
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体正日益被部署于科学研究领域，在这些场景中，可靠性至关重要，且底层知识高度互联。在这样的环境下，幻觉的危害尤为严重：关于某个基础概念的一条错误论断可能通过多步推理不断传播，从而破坏整条推理轨迹。现有的幻觉基准测试大多停留在表层，孤立地看待各个事实，并依赖忽略这种拓扑结构的统一准确率指标。我们用 SCHEMA 来填补这一空白——这是首个基于证据、拓扑感知的科学智能体幻觉评估框架。SCHEMA 自动从基准种子和文献证据构建科学概念图，合成涵盖论断验证、多跳推理、开放式解释和实验代码生成等多种基于图的任务，并以此对智能体进行评估。
tldr: 本文提出SCHEMA——首个基于证据、拓扑感知的科学智能体幻觉评估框架，通过自动构建科学概念图并生成论断验证、多跳推理、开放式解释与实验代码生成等多类图任务，捕捉幻觉在高度互联的科学知识网络中的级联传播效应。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces SCHEMA, the first evidence-grounded, topology-aware evaluation framework for scientific agent hallucinations, which automatically constructs scientific concept graphs and synthesizes graph-grounded tasks spanning claim verification, multi-hop reasoning, open-ended explanation, and experimental code generation to capture how hallucinations cascade through densely interconnected scientific knowledge.
